Asha Patel: FYI — AWS Marketplace payout for Feb shows a $23,412.67 shortfall vs our ledger. attaching the statement PDF to the thread and pasting the relevant CSV lines below. @Liam @Maya can you eyeball?

Liam O'Connor: On it. do we have the Marketplace invoice IDs and our internal invoice refs?

Asha Patel: Pasted snippet from the AWS statement CSV:```
InvoiceID,MarketplaceSKU,Amount,LineType
0987654321,aws_marketplace_reseller, -23412.67,ResellerAdjustment
0987654321,aws_marketplace_commission,  -1243.50,Commission
0987654321,aws_marketplace_fee,  0.00,ServiceFee
```

Maya Chen: :eyes: That `ResellerAdjustment` looks like a commit reconciliation credit. Could be AWS applying a committed usage offset after their settlement run.

reseller-sync-bot: Reconciliation job 2025-04-01T02:14Z completed: 482 invoices processed, 1 mismatch flagged -> invoice `0987654321`, external adjustment -$23,412.67.

Liam O'Connor: Can we map invoice `0987654321` back to a Dedicated commit or a marketplace purchase? If it's a reserved capacity refund, that needs different booking treatment.

Jorge Ramirez: I see a matching entry in our ledger: internal-ref `commit-2024-Q4-REDWOOD-PRD` shows a balancing line dated 2025-01-05 for $23,412.67 but tagged to GCP allocator. possible cross-cloud allocation error. Pulling raw ledger now.

Maya Chen: Also check our CSV parser rule: we recently had a change that treats any negative `LineType` as revenue reduction, but AWS sometimes uses `MarketplaceRefund` vs `ResellerAdjustment`. Parser might have misclassified this as revenue instead of contra-revenue.

Asha Patel: I'll re-run the importer with `--debug --invoice 0987654321` and paste the diff here.

Asha Patel: ```
[importer] loading invoice 0987654321
[importer] parsed line: ResellerAdjustment -> amount -23412.67 -> mapped to revenue_account=4000 (INCORRECT)
[importer] expected mapping: contra_revenue_account=4800
```

Liam O'Connor: If importer mapped it wrong, we can correct and re-run, but if AWS actually issued a negative adjustment on their statement the cashflow still doesn't match our payout. We'll need AWS support for clarification. @finance-leads?

Jorge Ramirez: I'll prep a packet: AWS statement PDF, our ledger extract, importer debug output, and the reconciliation job log. Recommend opening a case and asking AWS to confirm the `ResellerAdjustment` reason and whether it was applied to a Marketplace resettlement/commit balancing.

Maya Chen: Also worth checking GCP reseller statement for March — we had a few commit-level reallocations last quarter; don't want double-crediting across clouds.

Asha Patel: :thumbsup: Opening AWS case now. I'll assign to myself and cc `finance-ops@redwood.com`. Will escalate to legal if they push back. Holding booking of that $23,412.67 until resolved.

reseller-sync-bot: Ticket created: AWS case 1234567890 by Asha Patel. Status: OPEN.

Billing Bot: Reminder — Reserve capacity commit usage reconciliation job scheduled Thu 10:00 PT.

Liam O'Connor: Thanks everyone. Assigning to Jorge/Asha to triage. I'll note the variance in this month's close and follow up with accounting.

Asha Patel: Will keep updates here. If AWS response is delayed >72h, I'll escalate with the sample ledger and request a payout reissue or a detailed remittance breakdown.
